scope: Exodus 12–18, all 210 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew verse numbering align throughout Exodus 12–18.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Places the location before the speakers without adding a chronological transition.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt,
verses.after: In Egypt, the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt,

verses.rationale: Keeps both repeated calendar statements rather than compressing their institution into one.
verses.before: “This month will be for you the beginning of months; it will be the first month of the year for you.
verses.after: “This month will mark the beginning of your months. It will be the first month of your year.
verses.tsw_comparator: “This month shall be for you the beginning of months; it shall be the first month of the year for you.

verses.rationale: Seh includes a lamb or kid as verse 5 specifies; preserves male household representative and household scale.
verses.before: Speak to all the congregation of Israel, saying: On the tenth day of this month each household will take a lamb, a lamb for each household.
verses.after: Tell the whole community of Israel: On the tenth day of this month, each man is to take an animal from the flock for his family, one for each household.
verses.tsw_comparator: Speak to all the congregation of Israel, saying: On the tenth day of this month each household shall take a lamb, a lamb for each household.

verses.rationale: Unfolds allocation by persons and eating capacity while making the representative relationship explicit.
verses.before: And if a household is too small for a lamb, then the household and its nearest neighbor will take one according to the number of persons; according to what each person can eat you will make your count for the lamb.
verses.after: If a household is too small to eat one animal, its head and his nearest neighbor are to share one. Count the people and allow for how much each person will eat.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if a household is too small for a lamb, then the household and its nearest neighbor shall take one according to the number of persons; according to what each person can eat you shall make your count for the lamb.

verses.rationale: Preserves male age and unblemished condition, with both permitted species explicit.
verses.before: Your lamb will be without blemish, a male a year old; you may take it from the sheep or from the goats.
verses.after: The animal you choose must be a year-old male with no defect. You may take it from either the sheep or the goats.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male a year old; you may take it from the sheep or from the goats.

verses.rationale: Renders collective singular distributively, preserving communal slaughter; twilight represents the disputed between-the-evenings phrase.
verses.before: You will keep it until the fourteenth day of this month; then the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel will slaughter it at twilight.
verses.after: Keep it until the fourteenth day of this month. Then the whole assembly of Israel’s community is to slaughter their animals at twilight.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall keep it until the fourteenth day of this month; then the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall slaughter it at twilight.

verses.rationale: Keeps the three blood-marked doorway surfaces and eating location.
verses.before: Then they will take some of the blood and put it on the two doorposts and the lintel of the houses in which they eat it.
verses.after: They are to take some of the blood and put it on both doorposts and the lintel of the houses where they eat the animals.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they shall take some of the blood and put it on the two doorposts and the lintel of the houses in which they eat it.

verses.rationale: Retains all three meal elements and the night setting.
verses.before: They will eat the flesh that same night, roasted with fire; and they will eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
verses.after: That night they are to eat the meat roasted over a fire, along with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall eat the flesh that same night, roasted with fire; and they shall eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.

verses.rationale: Preserves the prohibited preparations and bodily completeness without specifying cleaning procedures absent here.
verses.before: Do not eat any of it raw or boiled in water, but roasted with fire—its head with its legs and its inner parts.
verses.after: Do not eat it raw or boiled in water. Roast it over a fire, with its head, legs, and internal organs.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not eat any of it raw or boiled in water, but roasted with fire—its head with its legs and its inner parts.

verses.rationale: Preserves the apparent repetition of prohibition and disposal instruction.
verses.before: You will let none of it remain until the morning; anything that remains until the morning you will burn with fire.
verses.after: Leave none of it until morning. Burn whatever is left by morning.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall let none of it remain until the morning; anything that remains until the morning you shall burn with fire.

verses.rationale: Makes girded loins concrete as clothing preparation while retaining sandals, staff, haste, and the named rite.
verses.before: This is how you will eat it: your belt fastened, your sandals on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and you will eat it in haste. It is the LORD’s Passover.
verses.after: Eat it with your clothes tucked into your belt, sandals on your feet, and your staff in your hand. Eat in haste. It is the LORD’s Passover.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is how you shall eat it: your belt fastened, your sandals on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and you shall eat it in haste. It is the LORD’s Passover.

verses.rationale: Retains divine first-person agency, lethal scope and gods as the stated objects of judgment without rationalization.
verses.before: For I will pass through the land of Egypt that night, and I will strike down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both human and animal; and on all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgments: I am the LORD.
verses.after: That night I will pass through Egypt and strike down every firstborn in the land, among both people and livestock. I will carry out judgments against all the gods of Egypt. I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I will pass through the land of Egypt that night, and I will strike down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both human and animal; and on all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgments: I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the sign for the addressed people and pesach word connection; protective force explained selectively in a note.
verses.before: The blood will be a sign for you on the houses where you are; when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague will be upon you to destroy you, when I strike the land of Egypt.
verses.after: The blood will be a sign for you on the houses where you are. When I see the blood, I will pass over you. No destroying plague will fall on you when I strike Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: The blood shall be a sign for you on the houses where you are; when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague shall be upon you to destroy you, when I strike the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Preserves remembrance, celebration, generational scope and binding ordinance.
verses.before: “This day will be a day of remembrance for you. You will celebrate it as a festival to the LORD; throughout your generations you will observe it as a perpetual statute.
verses.after: This day will be a memorial for you. Celebrate it as a festival to the LORD throughout your generations, a lasting ordinance.
verses.tsw_comparator: “This day shall be a day of remembrance for you. You shall celebrate it as a festival to the LORD; throughout your generations you shall observe it as a perpetual statute.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes leavening material from leavened food and retains cut-off sanction without choosing an unstated mechanism.
verses.before: Seven days you will eat unleavened bread. On the first day you will remove leaven from your houses; for whoever eats leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that person will be cut off from Israel.
verses.after: Eat unleavened bread for seven days. On the first day, remove the leaven from your houses. Whoever eats anything leavened from the first day through the seventh will be cut off from Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread. On the first day you shall remove leaven from your houses; for whoever eats leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that person shall be cut off from Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two sacred gatherings and narrow food-preparation exception.
verses.before: On the first day you will hold a holy assembly, and on the seventh day a holy assembly. No work will be done on those days, except what everyone must eat—that alone may be prepared by you.
verses.after: Hold a sacred assembly on the first day and another on the seventh. No work may be done on those days, except preparing the food each person needs to eat.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the first day you shall hold a holy assembly, and on the seventh day a holy assembly. No work shall be done on those days, except what everyone must eat—that alone may be prepared by you.

verses.rationale: Unfolds elliptical unleavened-bread observance; retains retrospective perfect inside anticipatory speech and military-group image.
verses.before: You will observe the Feast of Unleavened Bread, for on this very day I brought your divisions out of the land of Egypt. Therefore you will observe this day throughout your generations as a perpetual statute.
verses.after: Observe the Festival of Unleavened Bread, because on this very day I brought your divisions out of Egypt. Observe this day throughout your generations as a lasting ordinance.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall observe the Feast of Unleavened Bread, for on this very day I brought your divisions out of the land of Egypt. Therefore you shall observe this day throughout your generations as a perpetual statute.

verses.rationale: Keeps precise evening endpoints rather than replacing them with a generalized week.
verses.before: In the first month, from the evening of the fourteenth day of the month until the evening of the twenty-first day of the month, you will eat unleavened bread.
verses.after: In the first month, eat unleavened bread from the evening of the fourteenth day until the evening of the twenty-first.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the first month, from the evening of the fourteenth day of the month until the evening of the twenty-first day of the month, you shall eat unleavened bread.

verses.rationale: Preserves equal sanction for ger and native without softening exclusion or importing modern citizenship categories.
verses.before: For seven days no leaven will be found in your houses; for whoever eats what is leavened, that person will be cut off from the congregation of Israel, whether a resident alien or a native of the land.
verses.after: For seven days, no leaven is to be found in your houses. Anyone who eats leavened food will be cut off from Israel’s community, whether a resident foreigner or someone native to the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: For seven days no leaven shall be found in your houses; for whoever eats what is leavened, that person shall be cut off from the congregation of Israel, whether a resident alien or a native of the land.

verses.rationale: Retains concluding prohibition and positive command as separate emphases.
verses.before: You will eat nothing leavened; in all your dwellings you will eat unleavened bread.”
verses.after: Eat nothing leavened. Wherever you live, eat unleavened bread.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall eat nothing leavened; in all your dwellings you shall eat unleavened bread.”

verses.rationale: Preserves elders as recipients and family selection; renders Passover here as the animals sacrificed.
verses.before: Then Moses called all the elders of Israel and said to them, “Go, select lambs for your households, and slaughter the Passover lamb.
verses.after: Moses summoned all Israel’s elders and told them, “Go and choose animals from your flocks for your families, and slaughter the Passover animals.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses called all the elders of Israel and said to them, “Go, select lambs for your households, and slaughter the Passover lamb.

verses.rationale: Retains hyssop without speculative botanical identification and takes saf as basin, noting threshold alternative.
verses.before: Take a bunch of hyssop and dip it in the blood that is in the basin, and touch the lintel and the two doorposts with the blood in the basin. None of you will go out of the door of your house until the morning.
verses.after: Take a bunch of hyssop, dip it in the blood in the basin, and apply some of that blood to the lintel and both doorposts. None of you is to go out through the doorway of your house before morning.
verses.tsw_comparator: Take a bunch of hyssop and dip it in the blood that is in the basin, and touch the lintel and the two doorposts with the blood in the basin. None of you shall go out of the door of your house until the morning.

verses.rationale: Preserves the distinction between LORD and destroyer without adding an angel identification; doorway protection remains explicit.
verses.before: For the LORD will pass through to strike the Egyptians; when the LORD sees the blood on the lintel and on the two doorposts, the LORD will pass over that door and will not allow the destroyer to enter your houses to strike you.
verses.after: The LORD will pass through to strike Egypt. When he sees the blood on the lintel and both doorposts, he will pass over the doorway and will not let the destroyer enter your houses to strike you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD will pass through to strike the Egyptians; when the LORD sees the blood on the lintel and on the two doorposts, the LORD will pass over that door and will not allow the destroyer to enter your houses to strike you.

verses.rationale: Expresses generational banim inclusively while retaining perpetual obligation.
verses.before: You will observe this as a statute for you and for your children forever.
verses.after: Keep this instruction as an ordinance for you and your children forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall observe this as a statute for you and for your children forever.

verses.rationale: Preserves promised land and future observance rather than reducing it to commemoration alone.
verses.before: When you come to the land that the LORD will give you, as the LORD has promised, you will keep this observance.
verses.after: When you enter the land the LORD will give you as he promised, keep this observance.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you come to the land that the LORD will give you, as the LORD has promised, you shall keep this observance.

verses.rationale: Keeps the question directed to parents and lets the conditional sentence continue into its answer.
verses.before: And when your children say to you, ‘What do you mean by this observance?’
verses.after: When your children ask you, ‘What does this observance mean to you?’
verses.tsw_comparator: And when your children say to you, ‘What do you mean by this observance?’

verses.rationale: Maintains the parents’ our and third-person narrative return, with both striking and rescue intact.
verses.before: you will say, ‘It is the Passover sacrifice to the LORD, who passed over the houses of the Israelites in Egypt when he struck the Egyptians but spared our houses.’” And the people bowed down and worshiped.
verses.after: you are to say, ‘It is the Passover sacrifice to the LORD. He passed over the Israelites’ houses in Egypt when he struck the Egyptians, and he spared our homes.’” Then the people bowed down in worship.
verses.tsw_comparator: you shall say, ‘It is the Passover sacrifice to the LORD, who passed over the houses of the Israelites in Egypt when he struck the Egyptians but spared our houses.’” And the people bowed down and worshiped.

verses.rationale: Preserves emphatic obedience repetition instead of deleting it as redundant.
verses.before: Then the Israelites went and did so; just as the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron, so they did.
verses.after: The Israelites went and did what the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron. That is what they did.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the Israelites went and did so; just as the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron, so they did.

verses.rationale: Makes Pharaoh the enthroned referent and retains captive and livestock scope; no harm is euphemized.
verses.before: At midnight the LORD struck down all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat on his throne to the firstborn of the captive who was in the dungeon, and all the firstborn of the livestock.
verses.after: At midnight the LORD struck down every firstborn in Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh, who sat on his throne, to the firstborn of the captive in the dungeon, and every firstborn among the livestock.
verses.tsw_comparator: At midnight the LORD struck down all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat on his throne to the firstborn of the captive who was in the dungeon, and all the firstborn of the livestock.

verses.rationale: Retains universal household death claim and collective grief without apologetic qualification.
verses.before: Pharaoh rose up in the night—he and all his servants and all the Egyptians—and there was a great cry in Egypt, for there was not a house where there was not someone dead.
verses.after: Pharaoh got up that night, along with all his officials and all the Egyptians. A great cry rose through Egypt, for there was no house without someone dead.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pharaoh rose up in the night—he and all his servants and all the Egyptians—and there was a great cry in Egypt, for there was not a house where there was not someone dead.

verses.rationale: Retains abrupt commands and repeated serve vocabulary linking the demand and concession.
verses.before: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron by night and said, “Rise up, go out from among my people—both you and the Israelites. Go, serve the LORD, as you have said.
verses.after: That night he summoned Moses and Aaron and said, “Get up! Leave my people, both you and the Israelites. Go and serve the LORD, as you asked.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron by night and said, “Rise up, go out from among my people—both you and the Israelites. Go, serve the LORD, as you have said.

verses.rationale: Preserves complete livestock concession and Pharaoh’s personal request for blessing.
verses.before: Take your flocks and your herds, as you have said, and be gone. And bless me also.”
verses.after: Take your flocks and herds too, as you asked, and go. And bless me too!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Take your flocks and your herds, as you have said, and be gone. And bless me also.”

verses.rationale: Makes coercive urgency and feared death clear in direct speech.
verses.before: The Egyptians urged the people to hasten their departure from the land, for they said, “We will all be dead.”
verses.after: The Egyptians pressed the people to leave the land quickly. “We’ll all be dead!” they said.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Egyptians urged the people to hasten their departure from the land, for they said, “We shall all be dead.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the unleavened state and concrete bowls, wrapping and shoulder transport.
verses.before: So the people took their dough before it was leavened, with their kneading bowls bound up in their cloaks on their shoulders.
verses.after: So the people took their dough before it was leavened, carrying their kneading bowls on their shoulders, wrapped in their clothes.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the people took their dough before it was leavened, with their kneading bowls bound up in their cloaks on their shoulders.

verses.rationale: Uses anterior action to explain departure supplies; asked does not introduce an obligation to repay.
verses.before: The Israelites had done as Moses told them; they asked the Egyptians for objects of silver and gold, and for clothing.
verses.after: The Israelites had done as Moses told them: they had asked the Egyptians for silver and gold articles and clothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Israelites had done as Moses told them; they asked the Egyptians for objects of silver and gold, and for clothing.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine favor and forceful plunder conclusion without recasting it as a loan or erasing the image.
verses.before: And the LORD gave the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, so that the Egyptians granted their request. Thus they plundered the Egyptians.
verses.after: The LORD had made the Egyptians look favorably on the people, and they gave them what they asked for. So the Israelites plundered Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD gave the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, so that the Egyptians granted their request. Thus they plundered the Egyptians.

verses.rationale: Preserves approximate traditional number, specified males and separate dependents rather than silently recalculating population.
verses.before: The Israelites journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot—men, besides children.
verses.after: The Israelites traveled from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand men on foot, besides the children.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Israelites journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot—men, besides children.

verses.rationale: Retains mixed company without inventing ethnic identities and emphasizes livestock abundance.
verses.before: A mixed multitude also went up with them, and very many livestock, both flocks and herds.
verses.after: A large, mixed crowd also went up with them, along with flocks and herds—a great many animals.
verses.tsw_comparator: A mixed multitude also went up with them, and very many livestock, both flocks and herds.

verses.rationale: Keeps the narrative explanation and unprepared provisions without harmonizing away earlier ritual commands.
verses.before: They baked unleavened cakes of the dough that they had brought out of Egypt, for it was not leavened, because they were thrust out of Egypt and could not wait, nor had they prepared provisions for themselves.
verses.after: They baked the dough they had brought from Egypt into unleavened cakes. It had not been leavened because they were driven out of Egypt and could not delay; they had not even prepared provisions for themselves.
verses.tsw_comparator: They baked unleavened cakes of the dough that they had brought out of Egypt, for it was not leavened, because they were thrust out of Egypt and could not wait, nor had they prepared provisions for themselves.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned Hebrew’s Egypt location and 430 years; does not import the longer geographical reading of other witnesses.
verses.before: The time that the Israelites lived in Egypt was four hundred thirty years.
verses.after: The Israelites’ stay in Egypt lasted four hundred thirty years.
verses.tsw_comparator: The time that the Israelites lived in Egypt was four hundred thirty years.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated exact duration, emphatic day and divisions designation.
verses.before: At the end of four hundred thirty years, on that very day, all the divisions of the LORD went out from the land of Egypt.
verses.after: At the end of those four hundred thirty years, on that very day, all the LORD’s divisions left Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the end of four hundred thirty years, on that very day, all the divisions of the LORD went out from the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Maintains repeated watchfulness and LORD language without resolving the first phrase solely into divine or human vigil.
verses.before: It was a night of watching for the LORD, to bring them out of the land of Egypt; this same night is a night of watching kept to the LORD by all the Israelites throughout their generations.
verses.after: It was a night of watchfulness for the LORD as he brought them out of Egypt. This same night belongs to the LORD, a night for all Israelites to keep watch throughout their generations.
verses.tsw_comparator: It was a night of watching for the LORD, to bring them out of the land of Egypt; this same night is a night of watching kept to the LORD by all the Israelites throughout their generations.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes ben nekhar from resident foreigner admitted under verse 48, without turning the rite into an ethnic absolute.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “This is the statute of the Passover: no foreigner will eat of it.
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “This is the ordinance for Passover: No foreign outsider may eat it.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “This is the statute of the Passover: no foreigner shall eat of it.

verses.rationale: Names purchased slavery plainly and preserves circumcision prerequisite and male pronoun.
verses.before: But every slave who is bought for money may eat of it, after you have circumcised him.
verses.after: Any slave a man has bought with money may eat it once you have circumcised him.
verses.tsw_comparator: But every slave who is bought for money may eat of it, after you have circumcised him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two excluded social categories distinct from purchased slave and circumcised ger.
verses.before: No resident alien or hired worker will eat of it.
verses.after: A temporary resident or a hired worker may not eat it.
verses.tsw_comparator: No resident alien or hired worker shall eat of it.

verses.rationale: Retains single-house boundary and unbroken-bone prohibition without later interpretive application.
verses.before: It will be eaten in one house; you will not take any of the flesh outside the house, and you will not break any of its bones.
verses.after: It must be eaten in one house. Do not take any meat outside the house, and do not break any of its bones.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall be eaten in one house; you shall not take any of the flesh outside the house, and you shall not break any of its bones.

verses.rationale: Retains the community-wide obligation in concise English.
verses.before: All the congregation of Israel will keep it.
verses.after: The whole community of Israel is to observe it.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the congregation of Israel shall keep it.

verses.rationale: Makes household scope explicit from all males belonging to him and preserves admission and exclusion together.
verses.before: If a resident alien lives with you and would keep the Passover to the LORD, let all his males be circumcised; then he may come near and keep it; he will be like a native of the land. But no uncircumcised male will eat of it.
verses.after: If a foreigner living among you wants to observe Passover to the LORD, every male in his household must be circumcised. Then he may take part and will be treated like someone native to the land. No uncircumcised male may eat it.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a resident alien lives with you and would keep the Passover to the LORD, let all his males be circumcised; then he may come near and keep it; he shall be like a native of the land. But no uncircumcised male shall eat of it.

verses.rationale: Preserves one torah governing both categories within the Passover setting.
verses.before: There will be one instruction for the native and for the resident alien who lives among you.”
verses.after: The same instruction applies to the native and to the foreigner living among you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: There shall be one instruction for the native and for the resident alien who lives among you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated obedience formula aligned with 12:28.
verses.before: All the Israelites did just as the LORD commanded Moses and Aaron.
verses.after: All the Israelites did what the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron. That is what they did.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the Israelites did just as the LORD commanded Moses and Aaron.

verses.rationale: Maintains emphatic date, divine agency and grouped departure.
verses.before: And on that very day the LORD brought the Israelites out of the land of Egypt by their divisions.
verses.after: On that very day, the LORD brought the Israelites out of Egypt, division by division.
verses.tsw_comparator: And on that very day the LORD brought the Israelites out of the land of Egypt by their divisions.

verses.rationale: Uses a brief speech introduction without duplicating said and saying.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains womb-opening image and ownership; male scope becomes explicit in verses 12–15 rather than adding it twice here.
verses.before: “Consecrate to me every firstborn, whatever first opens the womb among the children of Israel, both human and animal. It belongs to me.”
verses.after: “Consecrate every firstborn to me. Whatever opens the womb among the Israelites, whether human or animal, belongs to me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Consecrate to me every firstborn, whatever first opens the womb among the children of Israel, both human and animal. It belongs to me.”

verses.rationale: Preserves remember, house of slavery and strong-hand image alongside the food command.
verses.before: Moses said to the people, “Remember this day on which you came out from Egypt, from the house of slavery, for by strength of hand the LORD brought you out from there. Nothing leavened will be eaten.
verses.after: Moses said to the people, “Remember this day, when you left Egypt, the house of slavery. The LORD brought you out of here with a strong hand. Nothing leavened is to be eaten.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said to the people, “Remember this day on which you came out from Egypt, from the house of slavery, for by strength of hand the LORD brought you out from there. Nothing leavened shall be eaten.

verses.rationale: Retains seasonal month name and present departure emphasis.
verses.before: Today you are going out, in the month of Abib.
verses.after: Today, in the month of Abib, you are leaving.
verses.tsw_comparator: Today you are going out, in the month of Abib.

verses.rationale: Preserves all five peoples, sworn gift, abundance image and calendrical recurrence.
verses.before: And when the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, which he swore to your ancestors to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, you will keep this service in this month.
verses.after: When the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites—the land flowing with milk and honey that he swore to your ancestors to give you—keep this observance in this month.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, which he swore to your ancestors to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, you shall keep this service in this month.

verses.rationale: Keeps full week and specified seventh-day festival.
verses.before: Seven days you will eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there will be a festival to the LORD.
verses.after: Eat unleavened bread for seven days, and on the seventh day hold a festival to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a festival to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated positive rule and territory-wide absence of both food and starter.
verses.before: Unleavened bread will be eaten for seven days, and nothing leavened will be seen with you, nor will leaven be seen with you within all your territory.
verses.after: Unleavened bread is to be eaten for those seven days. No leavened food or leaven is to be seen anywhere in your territory.
verses.tsw_comparator: Unleavened bread shall be eaten for seven days, and nothing leavened shall be seen with you, nor shall leaven be seen with you within all your territory.

verses.rationale: Retains singular son and personal identification with departure; supplies elliptical I do this rather than flattening into past history.
verses.before: You will tell your child on that day, saying, ‘It is because of what the LORD did for me when I came out from Egypt.’
verses.after: On that day tell your son, ‘I do this because of what the LORD did for me when I came out of Egypt.’
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall tell your child on that day, saying, ‘It is because of what the LORD did for me when I came out from Egypt.’

verses.rationale: Preserves bodily signs and mouth image without deciding physical versus figurative observance in main text.
verses.before: It will be for you as a sign on your hand and as a memorial between your eyes, so that the instruction of the LORD may be in your mouth, for with a strong hand the LORD brought you out from Egypt.
verses.after: It will be a sign on your hand and a reminder between your eyes, so that the LORD’s instruction may be in your mouth. For the LORD brought you out of Egypt with a strong hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall be for you as a sign on your hand and as a memorial between your eyes, so that the instruction of the LORD may be in your mouth, for with a strong hand the LORD brought you out from Egypt.

verses.rationale: Renders days-to-days recurrence naturally while retaining appointed timing.
verses.before: You will keep this statute at its appointed time from year to year.
verses.after: Keep this ordinance at its appointed time, year after year.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall keep this statute at its appointed time from year to year.

verses.rationale: Preserves conditional opening and lets the requirement continue in the next verse.
verses.before: “And when the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanite, as he swore to you and to your ancestors, and gives it to you,
verses.after: When the LORD brings you into the Canaanites’ land and gives it to you, as he swore to you and your ancestors,
verses.tsw_comparator: “And when the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanite, as he swore to you and to your ancestors, and gives it to you,

verses.rationale: Preserves womb-opening and explicit male restriction without collapsing the human redemption distinction that follows.
verses.before: you will set apart to the LORD everything that first opens the womb. Every firstborn male from your livestock belongs to the LORD.
verses.after: you must set apart for the LORD whatever first opens the womb. Every firstborn male among the animals you own belongs to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: you shall set apart to the LORD everything that first opens the womb. Every firstborn male from your livestock belongs to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps substitute species broad as seh, violent alternative explicit, and mandatory human redemption distinct.
verses.before: Every firstborn donkey you will redeem with a lamb, but if you do not redeem it, you will break its neck. Every firstborn among your sons you will redeem.
verses.after: Redeem every firstborn donkey with an animal from the flock. If you do not redeem it, break its neck. You must redeem every firstborn son of yours.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every firstborn donkey you shall redeem with a lamb, but if you do not redeem it, you shall break its neck. Every firstborn among your sons you shall redeem.

verses.rationale: Preserves father-son question, communal us and recurring strong-hand/slavery formula.
verses.before: And when your child asks you in time to come, saying, ‘What is this?’ you will say, ‘By strength of hand the LORD brought us out from Egypt, from the house of slavery.
verses.after: When your son asks you in days to come, ‘What does this mean?’ tell him, ‘The LORD brought us out of Egypt, the house of slavery, with a strong hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when your child asks you in time to come, saying, ‘What is this?’ you shall say, ‘By strength of hand the LORD brought us out from Egypt, from the house of slavery.

verses.rationale: Preserves explicit killed, Pharaoh’s agency, sacrifice/redemption contrast and male limitation.
verses.before: When Pharaoh hardened himself against sending us out, the LORD killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of humans to the firstborn of animals. Therefore I sacrifice to the LORD every male that first opens the womb, but every firstborn of my sons I redeem.’
verses.after: When Pharaoh stubbornly refused to let us go, the LORD killed every firstborn in Egypt, human and animal alike. That is why I sacrifice to the LORD every male that first opens the womb, but redeem every firstborn among my sons.’
verses.tsw_comparator: When Pharaoh hardened himself against sending us out, the LORD killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of humans to the firstborn of animals. Therefore I sacrifice to the LORD every male that first opens the womb, but every firstborn of my sons I redeem.’

verses.rationale: Retains concrete rare totafot object with restrained band rendering and explanatory note; keeps us in concluding reason.
verses.before: It will be as a sign on your hand and as bands between your eyes, for by strength of hand the LORD brought us out from Egypt.”
verses.after: It will be a sign on your hand and a band between your eyes, for the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand.”
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall be as a sign on your hand and as bands between your eyes, for by strength of hand the LORD brought us out from Egypt.”

verses.rationale: Preserves near-route concession and divine concern without diagnosing cowardice.
verses.before: When Pharaoh sent the people out, God did not lead them by the way of the land of the Philistines, though it was near, for God said, “Lest the people change their minds when they see war and return to Egypt.”
verses.after: When Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them by the road through the Philistines’ land, though it was near. God said, “If the people face war, they may change their minds and return to Egypt.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When Pharaoh sent the people out, God did not lead them by the way of the land of the Philistines, though it was near, for God said, “Lest the people change their minds when they see war and return to Egypt.”

verses.rationale: Retains indirect route, Yam Suph and traditional armed sense of hamushim, with uncertain expression noted.
verses.before: So God led the people around by the way of the wilderness toward the Sea of Reeds. The children of Israel went up armed from the land of Egypt.
verses.after: Instead, God led the people around by the wilderness road toward the Sea of Reeds. The Israelites went up from Egypt equipped for battle.
verses.tsw_comparator: So God led the people around by the way of the wilderness toward the Sea of Reeds. The children of Israel went up armed from the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Keeps doubled certainty and bones command, connecting the oath with Genesis 50 and divine attending vocabulary.
verses.before: Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, for Joseph had made the children of Israel swear solemnly, saying, “God will surely attend to you, and you will carry my bones up from here with you.”
verses.after: Moses took Joseph’s bones with him, because Joseph had made the Israelites swear an oath: “God will surely come to your aid. Then you must carry my bones up from here with you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, for Joseph had made the children of Israel swear solemnly, saying, “God will surely attend to you, and you shall carry my bones up from here with you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves exact two place names and wilderness boundary.
verses.before: They journeyed from Succoth and camped at Etham, at the edge of the wilderness.
verses.after: They traveled from Succoth and camped at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.
verses.tsw_comparator: They journeyed from Succoth and camped at Etham, at the edge of the wilderness.

verses.rationale: Keeps paired guidance/light functions and repeated day-night travel.
verses.before: The LORD went before them by day in a pillar of cloud to lead them on the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, so that they could travel by day and by night.
verses.after: The LORD went ahead of them in a pillar of cloud by day to guide them along the road, and in a pillar of fire by night to give them light. So they could travel by day and by night.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD went before them by day in a pillar of cloud to lead them on the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, so that they could travel by day and by night.

verses.rationale: Retains continual presence and position without introducing a new mover as explicit subject.
verses.before: The pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night did not depart from before the people.
verses.after: The pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night never left their place ahead of the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: The pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night did not depart from before the people.

verses.rationale: Keeps the speech transition concise and consistent with 13:1.
verses.before: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves all three place names and repeated positioning without asserting modern identifications.
verses.before: “Speak to the sons of Israel, that they turn back and camp before Pi-Hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, before Baal-Zephon. Opposite it you will camp by the sea.
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites to turn back and camp in front of Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, opposite Baal-zephon. Camp across from it, beside the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the sons of Israel, that they turn back and camp before Pi-Hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, before Baal-Zephon. Opposite it you shall camp by the sea.

verses.rationale: Renders Pharaoh’s report as thought and retains wilderness enclosure image.
verses.before: Pharaoh will say concerning the sons of Israel, ‘They are confused in the land; the wilderness has shut them in.’
verses.after: Pharaoh will think, ‘The Israelites are wandering in confusion. The wilderness has closed them in.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Pharaoh will say concerning the sons of Israel, ‘They are confused in the land; the wilderness has shut them in.’

verses.rationale: Preserves divine hardening and glory through the defeated army, then marks return to narrative.
verses.before: I will strengthen Pharaoh’s heart, and he will pursue them, and I will be honored through Pharaoh and through all his army. Then Egypt will know that I am the LORD.” And they did so.
verses.after: I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and he will pursue them. I will gain glory through Pharaoh and all his army, and the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD.” So the Israelites did as he said.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I will strengthen Pharaoh’s heart, and he will pursue them, and I will be honored through Pharaoh and through all his army. Then Egypt shall know that I am the LORD.” And they did so.

verses.rationale: Keeps reported flight distinct from permitted departure and economic motive rooted in service.
verses.before: When it was told to the king of Egypt that the people had fled, the heart of Pharaoh and his servants was turned toward the people, and they said, “What is this we have done, that we have sent Israel away from serving us?”
verses.after: When Egypt’s king was told that the people had fled, Pharaoh and his officials changed their minds about them. “What have we done?” they said. “We’ve let Israel go and lost their service!”
verses.tsw_comparator: When it was told to the king of Egypt that the people had fled, the heart of Pharaoh and his servants was turned toward the people, and they said, “What is this we have done, that we have sent Israel away from serving us?”

verses.rationale: Makes royal preparation natural without suggesting Pharaoh personally harnessed every component.
verses.before: So he harnessed his chariot and took his people with him.
verses.after: He had his chariot harnessed and took his troops with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he harnessed his chariot and took his people with him.

verses.rationale: Retains exact chosen force plus broader chariot force; officers does not claim a fixed third-rider arrangement.
verses.before: He took six hundred chosen chariots and all the chariots of Egypt, with officers over all of them.
verses.after: He took six hundred chosen chariots, along with all the other chariots of Egypt, with officers over them all.
verses.tsw_comparator: He took six hundred chosen chariots and all the chariots of Egypt, with officers over all of them.

verses.rationale: Preserves both explicit divine agency and the raised-hand departure image, explained in a note.
verses.before: The LORD strengthened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued the sons of Israel while the sons of Israel were going out with a high hand.
verses.after: The LORD hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued the Israelites as they went out with a raised hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD strengthened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued the sons of Israel while the sons of Israel were going out with a high hand.

verses.rationale: Keeps military components and repeated location, with camped Israelites clearly identified.
verses.before: The Egyptians pursued them—all Pharaoh’s horses and chariots, his horsemen, and his army—and overtook them camping by the sea, beside Pi-Hahiroth, before Baal-Zephon.
verses.after: The Egyptians pursued them—all Pharaoh’s chariot horses, horsemen, and army—and caught up with them where they were camped beside the sea, near Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Egyptians pursued them—all Pharaoh’s horses and chariots, his horsemen, and his army—and overtook them camping by the sea, beside Pi-Hahiroth, before Baal-Zephon.

verses.rationale: Keeps sudden sight, intense fear and appeal to God as a connected sequence.
verses.before: When Pharaoh drew near, the sons of Israel lifted their eyes, and look, Egypt was marching after them. They were very afraid, and the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD.
verses.after: As Pharaoh drew near, the Israelites looked up and saw the Egyptians marching after them. They were terrified and cried out to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Pharaoh drew near, the sons of Israel lifted their eyes, and behold, Egypt was marching after them. They were very afraid, and the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves bitter rhetorical question about graves and repeated accusation rather than summarizing it as complaint.
verses.before: They said to Moses, “Is it because there are no graves in Egypt that you have taken us away to die in the wilderness? What is this you have done to us by bringing us out from Egypt?
verses.after: They said to Moses, “Were there no graves in Egypt? Is that why you brought us out here to die in the wilderness? What have you done to us by bringing us out of Egypt?
verses.tsw_comparator: They said to Moses, “Is it because there are no graves in Egypt that you have taken us away to die in the wilderness? What is this you have done to us by bringing us out from Egypt?

verses.rationale: Retains their reported earlier speech and stark slavery/death comparison.
verses.before: Is this not the word that we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, ‘Leave us alone, and let us serve the Egyptians’? For it would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness.”
verses.after: Didn’t we tell you in Egypt, ‘Leave us alone! Let us serve the Egyptians’? It would be better to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Is this not the word that we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, ‘Leave us alone, and let us serve the Egyptians’? For it would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness.”

verses.rationale: Keeps see/today repetition and categorical future promise, with rescue concrete in context.
verses.before: Moses said to the people, “Do not fear. Stand firm and see the salvation of the LORD that he will work for you today. For the Egyptians whom you see today, you will never see again.
verses.after: Moses told the people, “Do not be afraid. Stand firm and see the rescue the LORD will bring you today. The Egyptians you see today—you will never see them again.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said to the people, “Do not fear. Stand firm and see the salvation of the LORD that he will work for you today. For the Egyptians whom you see today, you shall never see again.

verses.rationale: Keeps the contrast between divine fighting and human silence rather than adding effort-free spiritual application.
verses.before: The LORD will fight for you, and you will be silent.”
verses.after: The LORD will fight for you. You are to be still.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will fight for you, and you shall be silent.”

verses.rationale: Retains singular accusation to Moses even though his cry is not previously narrated.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses, “Why do you cry out to me? Speak to the sons of Israel, that they go forward.
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Why are you crying out to me? Tell the Israelites to move on.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses, “Why do you cry out to me? Speak to the sons of Israel, that they go forward.

verses.rationale: Preserves staff and hand as distinct instructions and the dry-ground route through the sea.
verses.before: And you, lift up your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it, so that the sons of Israel may go into the midst of the sea on dry ground.
verses.after: Lift your staff, stretch your hand over the sea, and split it, so that the Israelites can go into the sea on dry ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: And you, lift up your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it, so that the sons of Israel may go into the midst of the sea on dry ground.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine hardening of wider Egyptians and repeated glory/military scope.
verses.before: I, look, I will strengthen the heart of the Egyptians, and they will go in after them. I will be honored through Pharaoh and through all his army, through his chariots and through his horsemen.
verses.after: I am going to harden the Egyptians’ hearts, and they will go in after them. I will gain glory through Pharaoh and all his army, his chariots and his horsemen.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I, behold, I will strengthen the heart of the Egyptians, and they shall go in after them. I will be honored through Pharaoh and through all his army, through his chariots and through his horsemen.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated recognition and glory statement without deleting military repetition.
verses.before: Egypt will know that I am the LORD when I am honored through Pharaoh, through his chariots, and through his horsemen.”
verses.after: The Egyptians will know that I am the LORD when I gain glory through Pharaoh, his chariots and his horsemen.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Egypt shall know that I am the LORD when I am honored through Pharaoh, through his chariots, and through his horsemen.”

verses.rationale: Retains both angel and pillar movements without defining their relation more precisely than the text.
verses.before: Then the angel of God, who was going before the camp of Israel, moved and went behind them, and the pillar of cloud moved from before them and stood behind them,
verses.after: The angel of God, who had been going ahead of Israel’s camp, moved behind them. The pillar of cloud also moved from in front of them and stood behind them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the angel of God, who was going before the camp of Israel, moved and went behind them, and the pillar of cloud moved from before them and stood behind them,

verses.rationale: Preserves difficult darkness/light juxtaposition without supplying separate effects for each camp as explicit Hebrew.
verses.before: coming between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel. And there was the cloud and the darkness, yet it gave light by night, so that the one did not come near the other all night.
verses.after: It came between the Egyptian camp and Israel’s camp. There were cloud and darkness, yet it lit up the night. Neither camp came near the other all night.
verses.tsw_comparator: coming between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel. And there was the cloud and the darkness, yet it gave light by night, so that the one did not come near the other all night.

verses.rationale: Preserves east direction, all-night duration and LORD’s action through the wind.
verses.before: Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the LORD drove the sea back by a strong east wind all night and made the sea dry ground, and the waters were divided.
verses.after: Moses stretched his hand over the sea. All night the LORD drove the sea back with a strong east wind, turning it into dry ground. The waters split apart.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the LORD drove the sea back by a strong east wind all night and made the sea dry ground, and the waters were divided.

verses.rationale: Keeps dry ground and two-sided water wall as narrative images.
verses.before: And the sons of Israel went into the midst of the sea on dry ground, the waters being a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.
verses.after: The Israelites went into the sea on dry ground, with the waters forming a wall on their right and on their left.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the sons of Israel went into the midst of the sea on dry ground, the waters being a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.

verses.rationale: Maintains exhaustive military pursuit into the same sea route.
verses.before: The Egyptians pursued and went in after them into the midst of the sea—all Pharaoh’s horses, his chariots, and his horsemen.
verses.after: The Egyptians pursued them into the sea—all Pharaoh’s horses, chariots and horsemen.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Egyptians pursued and went in after them into the midst of the sea—all Pharaoh’s horses, his chariots, and his horsemen.

verses.rationale: Retains watch designation and pillar of both fire and cloud without assigning unsupported clock time.
verses.before: And in the morning watch the LORD looked down on the Egyptian forces from the pillar of fire and of cloud and threw the Egyptian forces into confusion,
verses.after: During the morning watch, the LORD looked down at the Egyptian camp from the pillar of fire and cloud and threw it into confusion.
verses.tsw_comparator: And in the morning watch the LORD looked down on the Egyptian forces from the pillar of fire and of cloud and threw the Egyptian forces into confusion,

verses.rationale: Follows pinned MT removal verb rather than emending to jammed; keeps Egyptian recognition of divine combat.
verses.before: clogging their chariot wheels so that they drove heavily. And the Egyptians said, “Let us flee from before Israel, for the LORD fights for them against Egypt.”
verses.after: He took off their chariot wheels, so they drove with difficulty. The Egyptians said, “Let’s flee from Israel! The LORD is fighting for them against Egypt!”
verses.tsw_comparator: clogging their chariot wheels so that they drove heavily. And the Egyptians said, “Let us flee from before Israel, for the LORD fights for them against Egypt.”

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated hand command and explicit targets of returning water.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the sea, that the waters may come back upon the Egyptians, upon their chariots, and upon their horsemen.”
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Stretch your hand over the sea so the waters return over the Egyptians, their chariots and their horsemen.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the sea, that the waters may come back upon the Egyptians, upon their chariots, and upon their horsemen.”

verses.rationale: Preserves difficult flight toward the returning water, full strength and forceful shook image without changing direction to ease tension.
verses.before: So Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to its normal course when the morning appeared. And as the Egyptians fled into it, the LORD threw the Egyptians into the midst of the sea.
verses.after: Moses stretched his hand over the sea, and as morning approached, the sea returned to its full strength. The Egyptians fled toward it, and the LORD shook them into the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to its normal course when the morning appeared. And as the Egyptians fled into it, the LORD threw the Egyptians into the midst of the sea.

verses.rationale: Retains total loss within the stated pursuing force and avoids an added claim about Pharaoh’s personal fate.
verses.before: The waters returned and covered the chariots and the horsemen; of all the host of Pharaoh that had followed them into the sea, not one of them remained.
verses.after: The waters returned and covered the chariots and horsemen—all Pharaoh’s army that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them remained.
verses.tsw_comparator: The waters returned and covered the chariots and the horsemen; of all the host of Pharaoh that had followed them into the sea, not one of them remained.

verses.rationale: Preserves full deliberate repetition from verse 22 in retrospective contrast.
verses.before: But the sons of Israel walked on dry ground through the sea, the waters being a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.
verses.after: But the Israelites had walked through the sea on dry ground, with the waters forming a wall on their right and on their left.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the sons of Israel walked on dry ground through the sea, the waters being a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.

verses.rationale: Retains hand idiom and visible dead bodies without softening the aftermath.
verses.before: Thus the LORD saved Israel that day from the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the seashore.
verses.after: That day the LORD rescued Israel from Egypt’s hand. Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the seashore.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus the LORD saved Israel that day from the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the seashore.

verses.rationale: Keeps hand motif and fear alongside trust, with Moses explicitly servant rather than a competing divine object.
verses.before: Israel saw the great power that the LORD used against the Egyptians, so the people feared the LORD, and they trusted in the LORD and in Moses his servant.
verses.after: Israel saw the mighty hand the LORD had used against Egypt. The people feared the LORD and trusted him and his servant Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: Israel saw the great power that the LORD used against the Egyptians, so the people feared the LORD, and they trusted in the LORD and in Moses his servant.

verses.rationale: Retains narrative introduction within verse paragraph and first-person song, emphatic elevation and horse/rider pair.
verses.before: Then Moses and the children of Israel sang this song to the LORD and said: “I will sing to the LORD, for he has risen in triumph; horse and rider he has thrown into the sea.
verses.after: Then Moses and the Israelites sang this song to the LORD: “I will sing to the LORD, for he has risen high in triumph; horse and rider he hurled into the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses and the children of Israel sang this song to the LORD and said: “I will sing to the LORD, for he has risen in triumph; horse and rider he has thrown into the sea.

verses.rationale: Retains short divine name and father singular; chooses traditional song/praise readings with alternatives noted.
verses.before: The LORD is my strength and my song, and he has become my salvation. This is my God, and I will praise him; the God of my father, and I will exalt him.
verses.after: Yah is my strength and my song; he has become my salvation. This is my God, and I will praise him; my father’s God, and I will lift him high.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD is my strength and my song, and he has become my salvation. This is my God, and I will praise him; the God of my father, and I will exalt him.

verses.rationale: Keeps masculine martial portrayal without replacing it with abstract victory or adding doctrine.
verses.before: The LORD is a warrior; the LORD is his name.
verses.after: The LORD is a warrior; the LORD is his name.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD is a warrior; the LORD is his name.

verses.rationale: Preserves parallel military groups and repeated sea with its Hebrew name.
verses.before: Pharaoh’s chariots and his army he cast into the sea; his chosen officers were sunk in the Sea of Reeds.
verses.after: Pharaoh’s chariots and army he cast into the sea; his chosen officers sank in the Sea of Reeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pharaoh’s chariots and his army he cast into the sea; his chosen officers were sunk in the Sea of Reeds.

verses.rationale: Keeps waters-depth repetition and stone simile for the sinking force.
verses.before: The deeps covered them; they went down into the depths like a stone.
verses.after: The depths covered them; they sank into the deep like a stone.
verses.tsw_comparator: The deeps covered them; they went down into the depths like a stone.

verses.rationale: Retains exact opening repetition and bodily right-hand image in parallel lines.
verses.before: Your right hand, O LORD, is majestic in power; your right hand, O LORD, shatters the enemy.
verses.after: Your right hand, LORD, is majestic in power; your right hand, LORD, shatters the enemy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your right hand, O LORD, is majestic in power; your right hand, O LORD, shatters the enemy.

verses.rationale: Preserves opponents rising, anger as consuming fire and agricultural stubble simile.
verses.before: In the greatness of your majesty you overthrow people who rise against you. You send out your burning anger; it consumes them like stubble.
verses.after: In your great majesty you overthrow those who rise against you. You send out your burning anger; it consumes them like stubble.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the greatness of your majesty you overthrow those who rise against you. You send out your burning anger; it consumes them like stubble.

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily wind image, heap, congealing and heart without rationalizing into a physical mechanism.
verses.before: At the breath of your nostrils the waters piled up; the floods stood upright like a wall; the deeps congealed in the heart of the sea.
verses.after: At the breath of your nostrils, waters piled up. Flowing streams stood like a heap; the depths congealed in the heart of the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the breath of your nostrils the waters piled up; the floods stood upright like a wall; the deeps congealed in the heart of the sea.

verses.rationale: Preserves rapid first-person boasts and desire/hand imagery; dispossess follows yarash causative without minimizing fatal context.
verses.before: The enemy said, ‘I will pursue; I will overtake; I will divide spoil. My appetite will be filled with them. I will draw my sword; my hand will dispossess them.’
verses.after: The enemy said, ‘I will pursue! I will overtake! I will divide the plunder; my desire will be filled with them. I will draw my sword; my hand will dispossess them.’
verses.tsw_comparator: The enemy said, ‘I will pursue; I will overtake; I will divide spoil. My appetite will be filled with them. I will draw my sword; my hand will dispossess them.’

verses.rationale: Keeps short divine answer to long boast and second sinking simile, lead distinct from stone.
verses.before: You blew with your breath; the sea covered them. They sank like lead in mighty waters.
verses.after: You blew with your wind; the sea covered them. They sank like lead in the mighty waters.
verses.tsw_comparator: You blew with your breath; the sea covered them. They sank like lead in mighty waters.

verses.rationale: Retains gods comparison and repeated rhetorical question without substituting angels or a doctrinal paraphrase.
verses.before: Who is like you among the gods, O LORD? Who is like you, majestic in holiness, awe-inspiring in praises, doing wonders?
verses.after: Who is like you among the gods, LORD? Who is like you, majestic in holiness, awesome in praises, doing wonders?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who is like you among the gods, O LORD? Who is like you, majestic in holiness, awe-inspiring in praises, doing wonders?

verses.rationale: Preserves earth-swallowing image instead of harmonizing it to sea-covered narration.
verses.before: You stretched out your right hand; the earth swallowed them.
verses.after: You stretched out your right hand; the earth swallowed them.
verses.tsw_comparator: You stretched out your right hand; the earth swallowed them.

verses.rationale: Retains hesed, redemption and completed-looking poetic movement without forcing a chronology.
verses.before: In your steadfast love you have led the people whom you redeemed. In your strength you have guided them to your holy dwelling.
verses.after: In your faithful love you led the people you redeemed; in your strength you guided them to your holy dwelling.
verses.tsw_comparator: In your steadfast love you have led the people whom you redeemed. In your strength you have guided them to your holy dwelling.

verses.rationale: Preserves collective nations and named region, with bodily gripping metaphor.
verses.before: Peoples hear; they tremble. Anguish seizes the inhabitants of Philistia.
verses.after: The peoples heard and trembled; anguish gripped those who live in Philistia.
verses.tsw_comparator: Peoples hear; they tremble. Anguish seizes the inhabitants of Philistia.

verses.rationale: Keeps three named peoples, distinct leaders and melting fear image.
verses.before: Then the chiefs of Edom are dismayed; the leaders of Moab— trembling seizes them. All the inhabitants of Canaan melt away.
verses.after: Then Edom’s chiefs were dismayed; Moab’s leaders were seized with trembling. All who live in Canaan melted away.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the chiefs of Edom are dismayed; the leaders of Moab— trembling seizes them. All the inhabitants of Canaan melt away.

verses.rationale: Preserves doubled until, arm, stone and acquired-people language without naming a route absent here.
verses.before: Terror and dread fall upon them. By the greatness of your arm they become still as stone until your people pass by, O LORD, until the people whom you acquired pass by.
verses.after: Terror and dread fall upon them. At the greatness of your arm, they are still as stone, until your people pass through, LORD, until the people you acquired pass through.
verses.tsw_comparator: Terror and dread fall upon them. By the greatness of your arm they become still as stone until your people pass by, O LORD, until the people whom you acquired pass by.

verses.rationale: Retains planting metaphor, mountain/inheritance and YHWH versus Adonai distinction without adding Zion identification.
verses.before: You will bring them in and plant them on the mountain of your inheritance, the place, O LORD, that you made for your dwelling, the sanctuary, O Lord, that your hands established.
verses.after: You will bring them in and plant them on the mountain of your inheritance— the place you made for your dwelling, LORD, the sanctuary your hands established, Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will bring them in and plant them on the mountain of your inheritance, the place, O LORD, that you made for your dwelling, the sanctuary, O Lord, that your hands established.

verses.rationale: Preserves perpetual kingship as the song’s close.
verses.before: The LORD will reign forever and ever.”
verses.after: The LORD will reign forever and ever.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will reign forever and ever.”

verses.rationale: Restores narrative prose after song, preserving both outcomes without merging verse into the poem.
verses.before: For Pharaoh’s horses went into the sea with his chariots and riders, and the LORD brought the waters of the sea back over them, but the children of Israel walked on dry ground among the sea.
verses.after: When Pharaoh’s horses, chariots and horsemen went into the sea, the LORD brought the sea’s waters back over them. But the Israelites walked on dry ground through the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: For Pharaoh’s horses went into the sea with his chariots and riders, and the LORD brought the waters of the sea back over them, but the children of Israel walked on dry ground in the midst of the sea.

verses.rationale: Names female prophetic role, stated sibling relation, all women and percussion without asserting metal jingles.
verses.before: Then Miriam the prophet, sister of Aaron, took a tambourine in her hand, and all the women went out after her with tambourines and dancing.
verses.after: Then Miriam the prophetess, Aaron’s sister, took a hand drum, and all the women went out after her with hand drums and dancing.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Miriam the prophet, sister of Aaron, took a tambourine in her hand, and all the women went out after her with tambourines and dancing.

verses.rationale: Keeps responsive action and refrain aligned exactly with verse 1 except plural imperative.
verses.before: Miriam answered them: “Sing to the LORD, for he has risen in triumph; horse and rider he has thrown into the sea.”
verses.after: Miriam sang in response to them: “Sing to the LORD, for he has risen high in triumph; horse and rider he hurled into the sea.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Miriam answered them: “Sing to the LORD, for he has risen in triumph; horse and rider he has thrown into the sea.”

verses.rationale: Preserves Moses’ leadership, named wilderness, three days and lack of water.
verses.before: Then Moses made Israel set out from the Sea of Reeds, and they went out into the wilderness of Shur. They went three days in the wilderness and found no water.
verses.after: Moses led Israel away from the Sea of Reeds into the wilderness of Shur. They traveled for three days in the wilderness and found no water.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses made Israel set out from the Sea of Reeds, and they went out into the wilderness of Shur. They went three days in the wilderness and found no water.

verses.rationale: Retains explanation of place name and undrinkable bitterness, with wordplay in note.
verses.before: They came to Marah, but they could not drink the waters of Marah because they were bitter. Therefore its name was called Marah.
verses.after: When they reached Marah, they could not drink its water because it was bitter. That is why the place was called Marah.
verses.tsw_comparator: They came to Marah, but they could not drink the waters of Marah because they were bitter. Therefore its name was called Marah.

verses.rationale: Preserves targeted grumbling and immediate question rather than moralizing thirst.
verses.before: The people murmured against Moses, saying, “What will we drink?”
verses.after: The people grumbled against Moses. “What are we to drink?” they asked.
verses.tsw_comparator: The people murmured against Moses, saying, “What shall we drink?”

verses.rationale: Specifies likely narrative agents, takes etz as wood, retains sweet and repeated there; no botanical remedy asserted.
verses.before: He cried out to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a piece of wood. He threw it into the waters, and the waters became sweet. There he made for them a statute and an ordinance, and there he tested them.
verses.after: Moses cried out to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a piece of wood. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. There the LORD gave the people a statute and a ruling, and there he tested them.
verses.tsw_comparator: He cried out to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a piece of wood. He threw it into the waters, and the waters became sweet. There he made for them a statute and an ordinance, and there he tested them.

verses.rationale: Preserves conditional address, eyes image and first-person disease/healing agency without general medical guarantees.
verses.before: He said, “If you will truly listen to the voice of the LORD your God, do what is right in his eyes, give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of the diseases upon you that I put upon Egypt, for I am the LORD who heals you.”
verses.after: He said, “If you listen carefully to the voice of the LORD your God, do what is right in his eyes, pay attention to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of the diseases on you that I put on Egypt. For I am the LORD who heals you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “If you will truly listen to the voice of the LORD your God, do what is right in his eyes, give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of the diseases upon you that I put upon Egypt, for I am the LORD who heals you.”

verses.rationale: Retains exact springs and palms counts and camp location.
verses.before: Then they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there by the waters.
verses.after: They came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and camped there beside the water.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there by the waters.

verses.rationale: Preserves whole community, distinct Sin/Sinai names and exact departure-relative date.
verses.before: They set out from Elim, and the whole congregation of the sons of Israel came to the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after their departure from the land of Egypt.
verses.after: They traveled on from Elim, and the whole community of Israelites came to the wilderness of Sin, between Elim and Sinai. It was the fifteenth day of the second month after they left Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: They set out from Elim, and the whole congregation of the sons of Israel came to the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after their departure from the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Retains whole-community complaint and both named recipients; written/read forms preserved in source hash.
verses.before: And the whole congregation of the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness,
verses.after: There in the wilderness, the whole community of Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the whole congregation of the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness,

verses.rationale: Preserves their idealized recollection as direct speech, divine hand and accusation of fatal starvation.
verses.before: and the sons of Israel said to them, “If only we had died by the hand of the LORD in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the pots of meat and ate bread to fullness; for you have brought us out into this wilderness to kill this whole assembly with hunger.”
verses.after: The Israelites said to them, “If only we had died by the LORD’s hand in Egypt, where we sat by pots of meat and ate bread until we were full! You have brought us into this wilderness to starve this whole assembly to death.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and the sons of Israel said to them, “If only we had died by the hand of the LORD in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the pots of meat and ate bread to fullness; for you have brought us out into this wilderness to kill this whole assembly with hunger.”

verses.rationale: Keeps bread-rain image and walk-in-instruction testing alongside daily provision.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Look, I am about to rain bread from heaven for you, and the people will go out and gather a day’s portion every day, that I may test them, whether they will walk in my instruction or not.
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “I am going to rain bread from heaven for you. Each day the people are to go out and gather that day’s portion. In this way I will test whether they will walk in my instruction or not.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Behold, I am about to rain bread from heaven for you, and the people shall go out and gather a day’s portion every day, that I may test them, whether they will walk in my instruction or not.

verses.rationale: Preserves sixth-day double portion and preparation rather than preempting the later Sabbath explanation.
verses.before: And on the sixth day, when they prepare what they bring in, it will be twice as much as they gather daily.”
verses.after: On the sixth day, when they prepare what they bring in, it will be twice as much as they gather each day.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And on the sixth day, when they prepare what they bring in, it will be twice as much as they gather daily.”

verses.rationale: Keeps evening recognition and divine rather than human agency.
verses.before: So Moses and Aaron said to all the sons of Israel, “At evening you will know that the LORD has brought you out of the land of Egypt,
verses.after: Moses and Aaron told all the Israelites, “This evening you will know that it was the LORD who brought you out of Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses and Aaron said to all the sons of Israel, “At evening you shall know that the LORD has brought you out of the land of Egypt,

verses.rationale: Retains morning/glory pairing and rhetorical who-are-we, with both complaint targets explicit.
verses.before: and in the morning you will see the glory of the LORD, because he has heard your grumbling against the LORD. For what are we, that you grumble against us?”
verses.after: In the morning you will see the LORD’s glory, because he has heard your grumbling against him. Who are we, that you grumble against us?”
verses.tsw_comparator: and in the morning you shall see the glory of the LORD, because he has heard your grumbling against the LORD. For what are we, that you grumble against us?”

verses.rationale: Supplies the prior knowledge clause to complete elliptical when-giving syntax; retains repeated question and explicit source contrast.
