verses.before: Moses said, “When the LORD gives you meat to eat in the evening and bread to fullness in the morning, because the LORD hears your grumbling that you grumble against him—what are we? Your grumbling is not against us but against the LORD.”
verses.after: Moses added, “You will know this when the LORD gives you meat to eat in the evening and all the bread you need in the morning, because he has heard the grumbling you direct at him. Who are we? Your grumbling is against the LORD, not against us.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Moses said, “When the LORD gives you meat to eat in the evening and bread to fullness in the morning, because the LORD hears your grumbling that you grumble against him—what are we? Your grumbling is not against us but against the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Preserves nested instruction through Aaron and coming before divine presence.
verses.before: Then Moses said to Aaron, “Say to all the congregation of the sons of Israel, ‘Come near before the LORD, for he has heard your grumbling.’”
verses.after: Moses told Aaron, “Say to the whole community of Israelites, ‘Come near before the LORD, because he has heard your grumbling.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses said to Aaron, “Say to all the congregation of the sons of Israel, ‘Come near before the LORD, for he has heard your grumbling.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps direction of gaze and sudden visible glory without specifying a form.
verses.before: And as Aaron spoke to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, they looked toward the wilderness, and look, the glory of the LORD appeared in the cloud.
verses.after: As Aaron spoke to the whole community of Israelites, they turned toward the wilderness, and there was the LORD’s glory, appearing in the cloud.
verses.tsw_comparator: And as Aaron spoke to the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, they looked toward the wilderness, and behold, the glory of the LORD appeared in the cloud.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated speech introduction aligned with earlier chapters.
verses.before: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains first-person hearing, twilight matching 12:6, full provision and covenantal identification.
verses.before: “I have heard the grumbling of the sons of Israel. Speak to them, saying, ‘At twilight you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be filled with bread. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God.’”
verses.after: “I have heard the Israelites’ grumbling. Tell them, ‘At twilight you will eat meat, and in the morning you will have your fill of bread. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: “I have heard the grumbling of the sons of Israel. Speak to them, saying, ‘At twilight you shall eat meat, and in the morning you shall be filled with bread. Then you shall know that I am the LORD your God.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves covering quail, surrounding dew and evening/morning sequence.
verses.before: In the evening quail came up and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a layer of dew around the camp.
verses.after: That evening quail came up and covered the camp. In the morning a layer of dew lay around the camp.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the evening quail came up and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a layer of dew around the camp.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated fine and frost simile while choosing flaky for uncertain texture term without identifying a natural substance.
verses.before: And when the layer of dew lifted, look, on the surface of the wilderness there was a fine, flake-like thing, fine as frost on the ground.
verses.after: When the layer of dew lifted, there on the wilderness surface was something fine and flaky, fine as frost on the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when the layer of dew lifted, behold, on the surface of the wilderness there was a fine, flake-like thing, fine as frost on the ground.

verses.rationale: Keeps question and explanatory ignorance repetition; man hu link to manna supplied in vocabulary.
verses.before: When the sons of Israel saw it, they said to one another, “What is it?” For they did not know what it was. And Moses said to them, “It is the bread that the LORD has given you to eat.”
verses.after: When the Israelites saw it, they asked one another, “What is it?” They did not know what it was. Moses told them, “This is the bread the LORD has given you to eat.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the sons of Israel saw it, they said to one another, “What is it?” For they did not know what it was. And Moses said to them, “It is the bread that the LORD has given you to eat.”

verses.rationale: Retains appetite allocation and per-person omer without reducing either to the other.
verses.before: This is the thing that the LORD has commanded: ‘Gather of it, each person of you, as much as he can eat. You will each take an omer, according to the number of persons that each of you has in his tent.’”
verses.after: This is what the LORD has commanded: Each of you is to gather as much as you need to eat—an omer for each person. Count the people in your tent and gather for them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the thing that the LORD has commanded: ‘Gather of it, each one of you, as much as he can eat. You shall each take an omer, according to the number of persons that each of you has in his tent.’”

verses.rationale: Preserves varied gathering amounts as separate from the measurement outcome.
verses.before: And the sons of Israel did so. They gathered, some more, some less.
verses.after: The Israelites did so. Some gathered more, some less.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the sons of Israel did so. They gathered, some more, some less.

verses.rationale: Keeps outcome without inserting redistribution or a miraculous resizing mechanism absent in verse.
verses.before: But when they measured it with an omer, whoever gathered much had nothing over, and whoever gathered little had no lack. Each of them gathered as much as he could eat.
verses.after: But when they measured it by the omer, those who gathered more had nothing left over, and those who gathered less had no shortage. Each had gathered what they needed to eat.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when they measured it with an omer, whoever gathered much had nothing over, and whoever gathered little had no lack. Each of them gathered as much as he could eat.

verses.rationale: Preserves categorical overnight restriction before later explicit exception.
verses.before: Moses said to them, “Let no one leave any of it over until the morning.”
verses.after: Moses told them, “No one is to leave any of it until morning.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Moses said to them, “Let no one leave any of it over until the morning.”

verses.rationale: Keeps disobedience, spoilage and Moses’ anger with men matching anashim.
verses.before: But they did not listen to Moses. Some left part of it till the morning, and it bred worms and stank, and Moses was angry with them.
verses.after: But they did not listen to Moses. Some men left part of it until morning, and it bred worms and stank. Moses was angry with them.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they did not listen to Moses. Some left part of it till the morning, and it bred worms and stank, and Moses was angry with them.

verses.rationale: Preserves daily repetition and heat-dependent melting.
verses.before: Morning by morning they gathered it, each as much as he could eat; but when the sun grew hot, it melted.
verses.after: Morning by morning they gathered it, each as much as they needed to eat. When the sun grew hot, it melted.
verses.tsw_comparator: Morning by morning they gathered it, each as much as he could eat; but when the sun grew hot, it melted.

verses.rationale: Retains doubled numerical measure, day and all leaders reporting.
verses.before: On the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread, two omers each, and all the leaders of the congregation came and told Moses.
verses.after: On the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread, two omers for each person. All the community’s leaders came and reported this to Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread, two omers each, and all the leaders of the congregation came and told Moses.

verses.rationale: Preserves intensified rest, holy Sabbath, two cooking methods and explicit storage exception.
verses.before: He said to them, “This is what the LORD has commanded: ‘Tomorrow is a day of solemn rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD; bake what you will bake and boil what you will boil, and all that is left over lay aside to be kept till the morning.’”
verses.after: He told them, “This is what the LORD said: Tomorrow is a complete rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD. Bake what you want to bake and boil what you want to boil. Set aside whatever remains and keep it until morning.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to them, “This is what the LORD has commanded: ‘Tomorrow is a day of solemn rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD; bake what you will bake and boil what you will boil, and all that is left over lay aside to be kept till the morning.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps exact contrast to ordinary-day spoilage and obedience reference.
verses.before: So they laid it aside till the morning, as Moses commanded them, and it did not stink, and there were no worms in it.
verses.after: They kept it until morning, as Moses had commanded. It did not stink, and there were no worms in it.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they laid it aside till the morning, as Moses commanded them, and it did not stink, and there were no worms in it.

verses.rationale: Retains threefold today rather than streamlining meaningful repetition.
verses.before: Moses said, “Eat it today, for today is a Sabbath to the LORD; today you will not find it in the field.
verses.after: Moses said, “Eat it today, because today is a Sabbath to the LORD. Today you will not find it in the field.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said, “Eat it today, for today is a Sabbath to the LORD; today you will not find it in the field.

verses.rationale: Keeps positive six-day gathering and absent seventh-day supply.
verses.before: Six days you will gather it, but on the seventh day, which is a Sabbath, there will be none.”
verses.after: Gather it for six days. On the seventh day, the Sabbath, there will be none.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Six days you shall gather it, but on the seventh day, which is a Sabbath, there will be none.”

verses.rationale: Preserves actual attempt and failure without adding motivations.
verses.before: On the seventh day some of the people went out to gather, but they found none.
verses.after: On the seventh day some of the people went out to gather, but they found nothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the seventh day some of the people went out to gather, but they found none.

verses.rationale: Marks plural rebuke within singular address to Moses; no claim that only Moses disobeyed.
verses.before: And the LORD said to Moses, “How long will you refuse to keep my commandments and my instructions?
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “How long will you all refuse to keep my commandments and instructions?
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD said to Moses, “How long will you refuse to keep my commandments and my instructions?

verses.rationale: Preserves Sabbath as gift, rationale and full spatial prohibition without importing later travel-distance rules.
verses.before: See, the LORD has given you the Sabbath; therefore on the sixth day he gives you bread for two days. Remain each of you in his place; let no one go out of his place on the seventh day.”
verses.after: See, the LORD has given you the Sabbath. That is why he gives you bread for two days on the sixth day. Each of you must stay where you are; no one is to leave their place on the seventh day.”
verses.tsw_comparator: See, the LORD has given you the Sabbath; therefore on the sixth day he gives you bread for two days. Remain each of you in his place; let no one go out of his place on the seventh day.”

verses.rationale: Retains Sabbath verb’s rest sense and the named day.
verses.before: So the people rested on the seventh day.
verses.after: So the people rested on the seventh day.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the people rested on the seventh day.

verses.rationale: Keeps house collective, food name, color, seed comparison and taste without asserting manna equals coriander.
verses.before: The house of Israel called its name manna. It was like coriander seed, white, and its taste was like wafers made with honey.
verses.after: The house of Israel called it manna. It resembled coriander seed. It was white and tasted like wafers made with honey.
verses.tsw_comparator: The house of Israel called its name manna. It was like coriander seed, white, and its taste was like wafers made with honey.

verses.rationale: Makes quotation level explicit so divine fed/brought agency is clear; preserves material memorial for descendants.
verses.before: Moses said, “This is the thing that the LORD has commanded: ‘Let an omer of it be kept throughout your generations, so that they may see the bread with which I fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you out of the land of Egypt.’”
verses.after: Moses said, “This is what the LORD has commanded: ‘Keep an omer of it for your generations to come, so they can see the bread I fed you in the wilderness when I brought you out of Egypt.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said, “This is the thing that the LORD has commanded: ‘Let an omer of it be kept throughout your generations, so that they may see the bread with which I fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you out of the land of Egypt.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps jar without adding gold and repeats measure and generational preservation.
verses.before: Moses said to Aaron, “Take a jar, and put an omer of manna in it, and place it before the LORD to be kept throughout your generations.”
verses.after: Moses told Aaron, “Take a jar, put an omer of manna in it, and place it before the LORD to be kept for your generations to come.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Moses said to Aaron, “Take a jar, and put an omer of manna in it, and place it before the LORD to be kept throughout your generations.”

verses.rationale: Retains testimony rather than importing ark into main text; note acknowledges anticipatory narrative reference.
verses.before: As the LORD commanded Moses, so Aaron placed it before the testimony to be kept.
verses.after: Aaron placed it before the testimony for safekeeping, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: As the LORD commanded Moses, so Aaron placed it before the testimony to be kept.

verses.rationale: Keeps retrospective forty years and repeated ate-manna endpoint clauses.
verses.before: The sons of Israel ate the manna forty years, until they came to a habitable land; they ate the manna until they came to the border of the land of Canaan.
verses.after: The Israelites ate manna for forty years, until they came to an inhabited land. They ate manna until they reached the edge of Canaan.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of Israel ate the manna forty years, until they came to a habitable land; they ate the manna until they came to the border of the land of Canaan.

verses.rationale: Preserves source’s own relative measure definition without an uncertain metric conversion.
verses.before: Now the omer is a tenth of an ephah.
verses.after: An omer is one-tenth of an ephah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the omer is a tenth of an ephah.

verses.rationale: Keeps commanded stages, named camp and genuine water shortage.
verses.before: All the congregation of the Israelites journeyed by stages from the wilderness of Sin, as the LORD commanded, and camped at Rephidim; but there was no water for the people to drink.
verses.after: The whole community of Israelites moved on from the wilderness of Sin, traveling stage by stage at the LORD’s command. They camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the congregation of the Israelites journeyed by stages from the wilderness of Sin, as the LORD commanded, and camped at Rephidim; but there was no water for the people to drink.

verses.rationale: Preserves quarrel/test distinction and two questions; English imperative does not force an additional addressee.
verses.before: So the people quarreled with Moses and said, “Give us water to drink.” Moses said to them, “Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test the LORD?”
verses.after: The people quarreled with Moses. “Give us water to drink!” they demanded. Moses said, “Why are you quarreling with me? Why are you testing the LORD?”
verses.tsw_comparator: So the people quarreled with Moses and said, “Give us water to drink.” Moses said to them, “Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test the LORD?”

verses.rationale: Retains striking collective us shifting to personal me/my instead of silently normalizing all plurals.
verses.before: But the people thirsted there for water; and the people complained against Moses and said, “Why did you bring us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our livestock with thirst?”
verses.after: The people were thirsty there and grumbled against Moses. “Why did you bring us up from Egypt,” they said, “to kill me, my children, and my livestock with thirst?”
verses.tsw_comparator: But the people thirsted there for water; and the people complained against Moses and said, “Why did you bring us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our livestock with thirst?”

verses.rationale: Preserves perceived immediate threat without narrating an actual stoning attempt.
verses.before: So Moses cried out to the LORD, “What will I do with this people? They are almost ready to stone me.”
verses.after: Moses cried out to the LORD, “What am I to do with these people? A little more, and they will stone me!”
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses cried out to the LORD, “What shall I do with this people? They are almost ready to stone me.”

verses.rationale: Retains staff attribution to Moses despite Aaron’s earlier action; does not silently harmonize distinct statements.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses, “Go on ahead of the people, and take with you some of the elders of Israel; take in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Go ahead of the people and take some of Israel’s elders with you. Take in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses, “Go on ahead of the people, and take with you some of the elders of Israel; take in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine standing on rock, strike instruction and elder witnesses without later allegory.
verses.before: See, I will be standing there before you on the rock at Horeb. Strike the rock, and water will come out of it, so that the people may drink.” Moses did so, in the sight of the elders of Israel.
verses.after: I will stand there before you on the rock at Horeb. Strike the rock, and water will come out for the people to drink.” Moses did this in the sight of Israel’s elders.
verses.tsw_comparator: See, I will be standing there before you on the rock at Horeb. Strike the rock, and water will come out of it, so that the people may drink.” Moses did so, in the sight of the elders of Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves both place names and their separate quarrel/test explanations with direct presence question.
verses.before: He called the place Massah and Meribah, because the Israelites quarreled and tested the LORD, saying, “Is the LORD among us or not?”
verses.after: He called the place Massah and Meribah, because the Israelites quarreled and tested the LORD, saying, “Is the LORD among us or not?”
verses.tsw_comparator: He called the place Massah and Meribah, because the Israelites quarreled and tested the LORD, saying, “Is the LORD among us or not?”

verses.rationale: Retains collective national name and precise battle location.
verses.before: Then Amalek came and fought with Israel at Rephidim.
verses.after: Then Amalek came and fought Israel at Rephidim.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Amalek came and fought with Israel at Rephidim.

verses.rationale: Preserves named Joshua, chosen men, tomorrow and staff ownership language.
verses.before: Moses said to Joshua, “Choose some men for us, and go out, fight with Amalek; tomorrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the staff of God in my hand.”
verses.after: Moses told Joshua, “Choose men for us and go out to fight Amalek. Tomorrow I will stand on top of the hill with God’s staff in my hand.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said to Joshua, “Choose some men for us, and go out, fight with Amalek; tomorrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the staff of God in my hand.”

verses.rationale: Keeps concurrent fighting and ascent with all three named men.
verses.before: So Joshua did as Moses told him, and fought with Amalek, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
verses.after: Joshua did as Moses told him and fought Amalek, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Joshua did as Moses told him, and fought with Amalek, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.

verses.rationale: Retains alternating advantage and singular hand rather than adding a prayer description.
verses.before: Whenever Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed; and whenever he lowered his hand, Amalek prevailed.
verses.after: Whenever Moses raised his hand, Israel had the upper hand. Whenever he lowered it, Amalek had the upper hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whenever Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed; and whenever he lowered his hand, Amalek prevailed.

verses.rationale: Preserves heavy-hands image, seated support, bilateral helpers and duration through sunset.
verses.before: Yet Moses’ hands grew weary; so they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on one side, and the other on the other side; so his hands were steady until the sun set.
verses.after: But Moses’ hands grew heavy. Aaron and Hur took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. They supported his hands, one on each side, so his hands stayed steady until sunset.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Moses’ hands grew weary; so they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on one side, and the other on the other side; so his hands were steady until the sun set.

verses.rationale: Retains military defeat and lethal weapon without inflating this verse into complete extermination.
verses.before: Joshua defeated Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
verses.after: Joshua defeated Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Joshua defeated Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.

verses.rationale: Preserves written memory and divine resolve to erase Amalek’s memory with full force and no sermon.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Write this as a remembrance in a book and recite it in the hearing of Joshua: I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.”
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “Write this in a scroll as a memorial, and make sure Joshua hears it: I will completely blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Write this as a remembrance in a book and recite it in the hearing of Joshua: I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.”

verses.rationale: Translates altar name transparently and retains commemorative act.
verses.before: Moses built an altar and named it, The LORD Is My Banner.
verses.after: Moses built an altar and named it “The LORD Is My Banner.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Moses built an altar and named it, The LORD Is My Banner.

verses.rationale: Keeps MT throne and short divine name, leaving whose hand and relation unresolved in main text; banner emendation only noted.
verses.before: He said, “A hand upon the throne of the LORD! The LORD will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.”
verses.after: He said, “A hand upon Yah’s throne! The LORD is at war with Amalek from generation to generation.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “A hand upon the throne of the LORD! The LORD will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.”

verses.rationale: Preserves Midianite priesthood, kinship and God/LORD naming in reported news.
verses.before: Jethro, priest of Midian, Moses’ father-in-law, heard all that God had done for Moses and for Israel his people, that the LORD had brought Israel out from Egypt.
verses.after: Jethro, the priest of Midian and Moses’ father-in-law, heard all that God had done for Moses and his people Israel—how the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jethro, priest of Midian, Moses’ father-in-law, heard all that God had done for Moses and for Israel his people, that the LORD had brought Israel out from Egypt.

verses.rationale: Retains passive dismissal with no invented timing, motive or divorce decision; sentence continues through sons.
verses.before: So Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, took Zipporah, Moses’ wife, after Moses had sent her away,
verses.after: Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, took Zipporah, Moses’ wife, after she had been sent away,
verses.tsw_comparator: So Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, took Zipporah, Moses’ wife, after Moses had sent her away,

verses.rationale: Keeps her sons relation, number two and personal foreigner explanation.
verses.before: and her two sons. The name of one was Gershom, for Moses had said, “I have been a resident alien in a foreign land.”
verses.after: along with her two sons. One was named Gershom, because Moses had said, “I have been a foreigner in a foreign land.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and her two sons. The name of one was Gershom, for Moses had said, “I have been a resident alien in a foreign land.”

verses.rationale: Retains father singular, help wordplay and sword rescue rather than generalized danger.
verses.before: The name of the other was Eliezer, for he had said, “The God of my father was my help and rescued me from Pharaoh’s sword.”
verses.after: The other was named Eliezer, because he had said, “My father’s God was my help and rescued me from Pharaoh’s sword.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The name of the other was Eliezer, for he had said, “The God of my father was my help and rescued me from Pharaoh’s sword.”

verses.rationale: Clarifies wife and sons belong to Moses and preserves wilderness mountain setting without chronology adjustment.
verses.before: Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, came with Moses’ sons and wife to Moses in the wilderness, where he was camped at the mountain of God.
verses.after: Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, came to Moses with Moses’ wife and sons in the wilderness, where he was camped at God’s mountain.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, came with Moses’ sons and wife to Moses in the wilderness, where he was camped at the mountain of God.

verses.rationale: Renders said as sent word from approach context, flags supplied communication manner in rationale; preserves first-person MT.
verses.before: He said to Moses, “I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you, and your wife and her two sons with her.”
verses.after: He sent word to Moses, “I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you with your wife and her two sons.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to Moses, “I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you, and your wife and her two sons with her.”

verses.rationale: Preserves bow, kiss, mutual welfare greeting and tent entry without interpreting bow as divine worship.
verses.before: Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, bowed down, and kissed him. They asked each other about their well-being and came into the tent.
verses.after: Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, bowed down, and kissed him. They asked about each other’s well-being and went into the tent.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, bowed down, and kissed him. They asked each other about their well-being and came into the tent.

verses.rationale: Keeps both victory report and actual hardship along the journey.
verses.before: Moses told his father-in-law all that the LORD had done to Pharaoh and to Egypt for Israel’s sake, all the hardship that had found them on the way, and how the LORD had rescued them.
verses.after: Moses told his father-in-law everything the LORD had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians for Israel’s sake, all the hardship they had met along the road, and how the LORD had rescued them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses told his father-in-law all that the LORD had done to Pharaoh and to Egypt for Israel’s sake, all the hardship that had found them on the way, and how the LORD had rescued them.

verses.rationale: Preserves joy, good and recurring hand-of-Egypt rescue image.
verses.before: Jethro rejoiced over all the good that the LORD had done for Israel, rescuing them from the hand of Egypt.
verses.after: Jethro rejoiced at all the good the LORD had done for Israel by rescuing them from Egypt’s hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jethro rejoiced over all the good that the LORD had done for Israel, rescuing them from the hand of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated rescue and hand clauses rather than reducing their liturgical force.
verses.before: Jethro said, “Blessed be the LORD, who rescued you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of Pharaoh, who rescued the people from under the hand of Egypt.
verses.after: Jethro said, “Blessed be the LORD, who rescued you from Egypt’s hand and Pharaoh’s hand, who rescued the people from under Egypt’s hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jethro said, “Blessed be the LORD, who rescued you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of Pharaoh, who rescued the people from under the hand of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Keeps gods comparison; supplies he prevailed and named referents to complete elliptical clause, with uncertainty explicitly noted.
verses.before: Now I know that the LORD is greater than all gods, for in the very thing in which they acted arrogantly, he was above them.”
verses.after: Now I know that the LORD is greater than all the gods, for he prevailed in the very matter in which the Egyptians acted arrogantly against Israel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now I know that the LORD is greater than all gods, for in the very thing in which they acted arrogantly, he was above them.”

verses.rationale: Preserves offerings and communal meal before God without assigning an unstated priestly officiant or adding Moses to diners.
verses.before: Then Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, took a burnt offering and sacrifices for God. Aaron and all the elders of Israel came to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law before God.
verses.after: Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, brought a burnt offering and sacrifices for God. Aaron and all Israel’s elders came to eat with him before God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, took a burnt offering and sacrifices for God. Aaron and all the elders of Israel came to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law before God.

verses.rationale: Keeps judicial sitting versus standing crowd and full-day duration.
verses.before: The next day Moses sat to judge the people, and the people stood around Moses from morning until evening.
verses.after: The next day Moses sat to judge the people, and they stood around him from morning until evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: The next day Moses sat to judge the people, and the people stood around Moses from morning until evening.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated observational question, alone and daily duration rather than a modern management summary.
verses.before: When Moses’ father-in-law saw all that he was doing for the people, he said, “What is this thing you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone while all the people stand around you from morning until evening?”
verses.after: When Moses’ father-in-law saw everything he was doing for the people, he asked, “What is this you’re doing for them? Why do you sit here alone while all the people stand around you from morning until evening?”
verses.tsw_comparator: When Moses’ father-in-law saw all that he was doing for the people, he said, “What is this thing you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone while all the people stand around you from morning until evening?”

verses.rationale: Keeps divine inquiry as Moses’ stated purpose, distinct from mere arbitration.
verses.before: Moses said to his father-in-law, “Because the people come to me to seek God.
verses.after: Moses answered his father-in-law, “The people come to me to inquire of God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said to his father-in-law, “Because the people come to me to seek God.

verses.rationale: Preserves dispute resolution and instruction as linked duties, rendering generic ish inclusively.
verses.before: When they have a matter, it comes to me, and I judge between one person and another and reveal the statutes of God and his instructions.”
verses.after: When they have a dispute, it comes to me. I judge between one person and another and make God’s statutes and instructions known to them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When they have a matter, it comes to me, and I judge between one person and another and make known the statutes of God and his instructions.”

verses.rationale: Keeps direct evaluation in simple speech.
verses.before: Moses’ father-in-law said to him, “The thing you are doing is not good.
verses.after: Moses’ father-in-law told him, “What you are doing is not good.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses’ father-in-law said to him, “The thing you are doing is not good.

verses.rationale: Retains emphatic exhaustion of both Moses and people, heavy burden and inability alone.
verses.before: You will surely wear yourself out, both you and this people who are with you, for the thing is too heavy for you. You are not able to do it alone.
verses.after: You and these people with you will surely wear out. This burden is too heavy for you; you cannot carry it alone.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will surely wear yourself out, both you and this people who are with you, for the thing is too heavy for you. You are not able to do it alone.

verses.rationale: Keeps counsel, blessing and Moses’ continuing representative task.
verses.before: “Now listen to my voice; I will counsel you, and may God be with you. You be for the people before God, and you will bring the matters to God.
verses.after: Now listen to me. I will advise you, and may God be with you. Represent the people before God and bring their matters to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Now listen to my voice; I will counsel you, and may God be with you. You be for the people before God, and you shall bring the matters to God.

verses.rationale: Preserves instruction, walking-way image and concrete doing rather than generic leadership language.
verses.before: Teach them the statutes and instructions, and reveal to them the way in which they will walk and the work they will do.
verses.after: Teach them the statutes and instructions. Show them the way they are to walk and the work they are to do.
verses.tsw_comparator: Teach them the statutes and instructions, and make known to them the way in which they shall walk and the work they shall do.

verses.rationale: Retains explicitly male selection, all four qualifications and all four numerical groupings without modernizing offices.
verses.before: But you will seek out from all the people capable men who fear God, people of truth who hate unjust gain. Place such over them as leaders of thousands, leaders of hundreds, leaders of fifties, and leaders of tens.
verses.after: Choose capable men from all the people—men who fear God, who are trustworthy and hate dishonest gain. Put them over the people as leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you shall seek out from all the people capable men who fear God, people of truth who hate unjust gain. Place such over them as leaders of thousands, leaders of hundreds, leaders of fifties, and leaders of tens.

verses.rationale: Keeps major/minor wording distinct from difficult in verse 26 and shared burden image.
verses.before: Let them judge the people at all times. Every great matter they will bring to you, but every small matter they will judge themselves. Make it lighter for yourself, and let them carry the burden with you.
verses.after: Let them judge the people at all times. They are to bring every major matter to you, but judge every minor matter themselves. Lighten your load this way, and let them carry it with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let them judge the people at all times. Every great matter they shall bring to you, but every small matter they shall judge themselves. Make it lighter for yourself, and let them carry the burden with you.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine-command condition rather than treating advice as automatically authorized; keeps stand and peace.
verses.before: If you do this thing and God commands you, then you will be able to endure, and all this people also will go to their place in peace.”
verses.after: If you do this, and God commands you to, you will be able to stand, and all these people will go home in peace.”
verses.tsw_comparator: If you do this thing and God commands you, then you will be able to endure, and all this people also will go to their place in peace.”

verses.rationale: Keeps both hearing and enacted response.
verses.before: Moses listened to the voice of his father-in-law and did all that he had said.
verses.after: Moses listened to his father-in-law and did everything he said.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses listened to the voice of his father-in-law and did all that he had said.

verses.rationale: Retains men and exact four-tier repetition in implementation.
verses.before: Moses chose capable men from all Israel and made them heads over the people: leaders of thousands, leaders of hundreds, leaders of fifties, and leaders of tens.
verses.after: Moses chose capable men from all Israel and made them heads over the people, leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses chose capable men from all Israel and made them heads over the people: leaders of thousands, leaders of hundreds, leaders of fifties, and leaders of tens.

verses.rationale: Keeps difficult rather than major, preserving variation from proposed arrangement.
verses.before: They judged the people at all times. The difficult matter they brought to Moses, but every small matter they judged themselves.
verses.after: They judged the people at all times. They brought the difficult matters to Moses and judged every minor matter themselves.
verses.tsw_comparator: They judged the people at all times. The difficult matter they brought to Moses, but every small matter they judged themselves.

verses.rationale: Clarifies departure referent without adding a destination city or time interval.
verses.before: Then Moses sent his father-in-law away, and he went to his own land.
verses.after: Then Moses sent his father-in-law on his way, and Jethro returned to his own land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses sent his father-in-law away, and he went to his own land.
